summary: Cross-functional secondment exit — KMS key owner transfer, device escrow, and temporary admin handoff
access_to_remove: GitHub - maya-patel (org membership and repo access)
description:
Issue summary: Maya Patel is exiting Redwood for a 6-month cross-functional secondment to a partner org (starts 2026-02-20). HR has requested a controlled exit handoff that both removes unnecessary day-to-day privileges and transfers ownership/responsibility for a production KMS key used by 'analytics-pipeline-prod'. We also need to escrow the company laptop and ensure hardware credentials (YubiKey) are rotated/re-assigned securely.

Background: Maya currently holds owner binding on a customer-facing KMS key (projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/analytics-prod-key) used by the analytics ingestion job. She will be physically returning the laptop and YubiKey but will require transient elevated access for 48 hours during the handoff window to transfer key bindings and verify service continuity.

Impact: If KMS owner transfer is done incorrectly, analytics ingestion could lose ability to decrypt keys and cause downstream failures for internal dashboards. Leaving hardware un-escrowed or not rotating keys risks credential leakage. We must avoid a full immediate deprovision that would break running jobs.

Requested actions: 1) Approve a 48-hour temporary admin elevation policy exception for Maya scoped only to KMS key bindings and service account role assignments (dates 2026-02-18 to 2026-02-20). 2) Create a formal KMS ownership transfer plan and execute with audit logging. 3) Escrow the laptop and YubiKey to Secure Locker (Asset tag: AL-5302) and update asset-inventory. 4) Rotate any service account keys that were directly known to Maya and confirm CI/CD tokens are re-keyed. 5) After transfer, remove Maya's org-level admin and deprovision SSO accounts per offboarding runbook.

Proposed timeline:
- 2026-02-16: SRE & Security review transfer plan and approve temporary elevation scope.
- 2026-02-18 09:00 UTC: Grant scoped elevation. Maya performs transfer with SRE on-call in session.
- 2026-02-18 16:00 UTC: Verify ingestion jobs, run smoke tests, confirm metrics.
- 2026-02-20: Revoke elevation, update asset-inventory and close ticket.

Dependencies: HR sign-off (exit checklist), Security approval for temporary elevation (SEC), SRE availability during transfer window, access to Secure Locker at HQ for physical device drop-off.

Questions for policy: Is a scoped 48-hour KMS owner transfer exception acceptable under current KMS ownership policy, or do we need a formal change request and multi-person approval flow? If policy requires, should we instead perform a service account rotation without transferring key owner bindings?

Additional context: Maya has raised concern that some legacy ingestion tasks reference her personal service account; we suspect there are 2-3 CI jobs to update. See logs: gcs://redwood-ops/logs/ingest/2026-02-09/* for recent failures that mention 'permission denied' when simulating reduced bindings.
steps_to_reproduce: This is an offboarding workflow rather than a software bug; steps to validate safe transfer: 1) Create a test key in staging and practice the owner binding transfer with audit logging enabled. 2) Run analytics ingestion on staging with service account rotated to new owner and confirm decryption and job success. 3) Run smoke tests for dashboards relying on the pipeline. 4) Validate asset check-in process by escrowing a device in Secure Locker and updating asset-inventory entry.
investigation_notes:
SRE initial check (2026-02-11): Found three deployments referencing service account 'svc-maya-ingest' in infra repo. Security ran a dry-run of KMS IAM policy delta; transfer requires removing 'roles/cloudkms.admin' for maya.p@redwood.ai and adding 'roles/cloudkms.admin' to a new team service account 'svc-ingest-owners@redwood.ai'. Audit logs show recent key usage by the ingestion service account, not directly by Maya's user account, which reduces risk.
Hypothesis: Transfer can be executed by creating a team-level service account and migrating bindings, followed by rotating any short-lived keys. This avoids giving long-lived owner role to an individual during secondment.

Notes from HR (2026-02-10): Asset return window scheduled 2026-02-19; Maya requested to complete transfer before physical return.

2026-02-10 - Anika Shah (Assignee): Acknowledged. I'll coordinate with Security and SRE to draft the transfer plan. Tentative SRE on-call: @sre-oncall-2.

2026-02-11 - Rajiv Menon (Security): Security approves scoped temporary elevation if session is recorded, MFA is enforced, and two-person approval is logged in IAM change. Please add proposed times and the new team service account name.

2026-02-11 - Priya Desai (HR): Confirmed exit checklist. Secure Locker booking AL-5302 reserved for 2026-02-19 15:00. HR will accept device only after this ticket confirms KMS ownership changes are complete.

2026-02-12 - Anika Shah: Drafted transfer plan and attached to repo PR for infra changes. Waiting on Security to confirm they will be present during handoff. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8273
resolution_notes: Partial workaround executed 2026-02-12: Created team service account 'svc-ingest-owners@redwood.ai' and pre-provisioned its KMS bindings in a locked change set. Security approved recording of the transfer session. Full transfer scheduled for 2026-02-18. Post-transfer actions: rotate any service account credentials referenced directly by Maya, update infra PR, and close ticket.
related_policy_question: Does current KMS policy permit temporary individual owner bindings for offboarding handoffs, or must ownership always be with a team/service account? If the latter, please confirm the documented minimum approver set for transfers.
notes_for_follow_up: After transfer and device escrow, schedule a retrospective to confirm runbook adequacy and identify automation opportunities: auto-detect user-scoped KMS bindings and recommend team-service-account replacements.
